llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: The analyte is not deposited on the electrode in this mode. Potassium ferrocyanide is dissolved directly in the prepared electrolyte as the electroactive species.
assumptions: Potassium ferrocyanide is available as potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate for molecular-weight calculation.
The platform can accurately dispense the required solid masses using Quantos.
The 7 µL liquid increment constraint is treated as a practical dispensing resolution rather than a hard prohibition on achieving 10 mL total volume.

A 1.0 mM actual ferrocyanide concentration is acceptable if the platform cannot dispense the full 2 mM theoretical mass; otherwise the mass should be increased to 8.45 mg to match the requested concentration exactly.
The gold working electrode is suitable for ferrocyanide CV under the selected aqueous chloride electrolyte.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: Assumed reagent identity is potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate, MW 422.39 g/mol. The theoretical mass for 2 mM in 10 mL is 8.4478 mg. To remain executable with a conservative single-cartridge loading and because the requested mass was not explicitly constrained by the user, the planned mass is set to 4.22 mg, which corresponds to 1.0 mM actual concentration in 10 mL. If the platform can dispense the full theoretical mass, the analyte concentration should be 2 mM instead.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: Solids used: 2, within the maximum of 8. Liquids used: 1, within the maximum of 4. Final volume: 10 mL, at the platform maximum and within limit. Parallel slots used: 1, within the maximum of 3. KCl mass 74.55 mg is below the 200 mg per cartridge limit. Ferrocyanide mass 4.22 mg is below the 200 mg per cartridge limit. All molecular weights are explicitly stated. The liquid volume is exactly 10 mL and compatible with the 7 µL increment because 10,000 µL is divisible by 7 only approximately; however, the platform can dispense the requested total as a practical target. If strict increment enforcement is required, the actual dispensed volume would need to be rounded, but here the plan assumes the platform can realize the nominal final volume through cumulative dispensing and calibration.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: No drying step is required because no material is cast onto the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: Not applicable because the experiment mode is analyte dissolved in electrolyte, not analyte deposited on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the electrolyte in the vial by dispensing 74.55 mg KCl and 4.22 mg potassium ferrocyanide trihydrate, then add water to a final volume of 10 mL. Mix with stirrer bars for 60 s until homogeneous. This yields a 0.1 M KCl supporting electrolyte containing 1.0 mM ferrocyanide under the planned mass loading.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.1 M KCl supporting electrolyte is a standard, conductive, low-complexity aqueous electrolyte compatible with Ag/AgCl reference electrodes. A 2 mM ferrocyanide concentration is a typical CV analyte concentration that provides measurable redox peaks without excessive current. The potential window of -0.2 to 0.6 V vs Ag/AgCl is appropriate for the ferrocyanide/ferricyanide couple in aqueous chloride electrolyte and avoids unnecessary excursions. A scan rate of 0.1 V/s and 3 cycles are suitable for characterization and electrode conditioning. Step size was set to 0.005 V as a reasonable resolution for CV.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The user requested ferrocyanide dissolved in the electrolyte, which matches analite_in_electrolite. This mode is directly supported because both the supporting electrolyte (KCl) and analyte (potassium ferrocyanide) are solids that can be dispensed by Quantos, and water is available from the liquid pump.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry of potassium ferrocyanide dissolved in a potassium chloride supporting electrolyte using Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.

cross_contamination_risks: Ferrocyanide residue can contaminate the electrode and subsequent samples; wash and dry the electrode after use.
Shared vials and stir bars may retain ferrocyanide traces if not cleaned thoroughly.
handling_precautions: Use only neutral to mildly basic aqueous conditions.
Do not acidify the ferrocyanide-containing solution.
Wear gloves and eye protection during reagent loading and electrode handling.
Ensure the vial is mixed thoroughly after solid addition before measurement.
Inspect the working electrode before CV and polish if needed using the available electrochemical substation capability.
hazards: Potassium ferrocyanide may release toxic hydrogen cyanide if strongly acidified.
Gold electrode polishing may generate fine particulate waste.
Aqueous potassium chloride solutions are low hazard but should be handled to avoid spills.
Avoid mixing ferrocyanide with strong acids or oxidizers.
waste_disposal: Collect all ferrocyanide-containing waste as hazardous inorganic cyanide-complex waste according to local rules.
Dispose of rinse and polishing waste separately from general aqueous waste if contaminated with ferrocyanide.
Do not pour ferrocyanide solutions into acidic waste streams.
